title: Johnny; or, The Little Cripple' Song
author: Root, George F. (George Frederick), 1820-1895
verses:
We passed poor Johnny's cabin,
The evening sun was low,
And thro' the little window
It sent its parting glow;
His patient eyes were resting
Upon the open door,
And, while we listened, sweetly came
This burden o'er and o'er.

His old and well-worn Bible
Was close beside his bed,
The golden hues of sunset
Were playing round his head;
A radiance more than earthly
Beamed from his features thin,
We paused to hear his song again
Before we entered in.

But when we came to leave him,
And held his slender hand, 
We knew he had a comfort
We could not understand;
And as beneath the maple
We stopped again to hear,
There seemed a sound of angels in
The song so heav'nly clear.
chorus:
I love him, oh, I love him,
My Saviour near and dear,
For tho' he cares for countless worlds,
He's always with me here.
O Savior, blessed Savior,
My heart is filled with joy,
How can you stay, and love me so,
A little crippled boy?

title: Join all the glorious names

Join all the glorious Names

That ever Mortal knew,
That Angels ever bore:

To speak his Worth,
Too mean to set
My Saviour forth.

But O what gentle Terms,
What condescending Ways
Doth our Redeemer use
To teach his heav'nly Grace!
Mine Eyes with Joy
And Wonder see
What Forms of Love
He bears for me.

Array'd in mortal Flesh,
He like an Angel stands,
And holds the Promises
And Pardons in his Hands;
Commission'd from
His Father's Throne,
To make his Grace
To Mortals known.]

Great Prophet of my God,
My Tongue would bless thy Name;
By Thee the joyful News
Of our Salvation came;
The joyful News
Of Sins forgiv'n,
Of Hell subdu'd,
And peace with Heav'n.]

Be thou my Counsellor,
My Pattern, and my Guide;
And through this desart Land
Still keep me near thy Side.
O let my Feet
Ne'er run astray,
Nor rove, nor seek
The crooked Way!]

I love my Shepherd's Voice,
His watchful Eyes shall keep
My wand'ring Soul among
The Thousands of his Sheep:
He feeds his Flock,
He calls their Names,
His Bosom bears
The tender Lambs.]

To this dear Surety's Hand
Will I commit my Cause;
He answers and fulfills
His Father's broken Laws.
Behold my Soul
At freedom set!
My Surety paid
The dreadful Debt.]

Jesus, my great High-Priest,
Offer'd his Blood and dy'd;
My guilty Conscience seeks
No Sacrifice beside.
His pow'rful Blood
Did once atone?
And now it pleads
Before the Throne.]

My Advocate appears
For my Defence on high;
The Father bows his Ears,
And lays his Thunder by.
Not all that Hell
Or Sin can say
Shall turn his Heart,
His Love, away.]

Thy Scepter, and thy Sword,
Thy reigning Grace I sing.
Thine is the Pow'r;
Behold I sit
In willing Bonds

Now let my Soul arise,
And tread the Tempter down;
My Captain leads me forth
To Conquest and a Crown.
A feeble Saint
Shall win the Day,
Though Death and Hell
Obstruct the Way.]

Should all the Hosts of Death,
And Pow'rs of Hell unknown,
Put their most dreadful Forms
Of Rage and Mischief on;
I shall be safe,
For Christ displays
Superior Pow'r,
And Guardian Grace

Join all thy Powers, O my Soul,
God's holy Name to bless.
2. The Lord bless, O my Soul; forget
None of his Acts of Grace.
3. 'Tis he doth all thy Sins forgive;
And Sicknesses remove.
4. He from the Grave redeems thy Life;
And crowns thee with his Love.

He fills thy Mouth with Good; thy Youth,
As th' Eagle's, he renews.
6. Judgment, and Justice, for th' Oppress'd,
The Lord himself pursues.
7. His Ways, to Moses, he made known;
His Acts to Isr'el's Race.
8. The Lord is good, and kind; he's slow
To Wrath, but full of Grace.

He will not always chide; nor mark
Forever, when we swerve.
10. He chastens not for ev'ry Crime;
For none as we deserve.
11. The Height of Heav'n's extended Arch
Above this early Frame,
Is far exceeded by his Grace,
To them that fear his Name.

Far as the East is from the West;
So far, his pard'ning Love
Doth, our Transgressions manifold,
Distant, from us, remove.
Second Part

A Father pities his young Son;
So doth the Lord the Just.
14. He knows how feeble is our Frame,
Remembers we are Dust.
15. Man's Days like Grass; he flourisheth,
As a Field-Flow'r new blown.
16. The Wind sweeps o'er, it disappears;
It's Place no more is known.

But, Lord, thy Mercy ever was,
And ever will endure,
To them that fear Thee; and thy Truth
To Children's Children's sure:
18. To such as keep his covenant,
And his commands obey.
19. The Lord, in Heav'n prepar'd his Throne;
O'er all extends his Sway.

Ye holy Angels, mighty Pow'rs,
Bless ye Jehovah still;
Who hear his Voice attentively,
And constant do his Will.
21. Bless God, his Hosts, and Ministers,
That do his Pleasure whole.
22. Thro' his wide Empire, bless the Lord;
The Lord bless, O my Soul.

title: Joining the Church
author: Godwin, Edward
verses:
Welcome, thou well belov'd of God,
Thou heir of grace redeem'd by blood;
Welcome with us thy hand to join,
As partner of our lot divine:
Abundant blessings from above,
Give him, we pray, thou God of love.

With us the pilgrim's state embrace;
We're trav'lling to a blissful place,
The new Jerusalem above,
The radiant throne, the seat, of love.
The Holy Ghost that knows the way,
Conduct thee on from day to day!

The staff of promise now receive,
The weary footsteps to relieve,
The chief support the tra'vler knows,
Leaning on which he forward goes.
Thus if for rest thy spirits call,
Leaning on which he cannot fall.

With peace, with ceaseless peace beshod,
The shoes of peace receive of God;
These keep from pain the pilgrim's feet,
And make the rugged way see sweet.
So Sion's paths shall ever prove,
The paths of joy, and peace and love.

Thus onward move with upright pace;
Stedfast pursue the gospel race:
Fill'd with the power of truth divine,
Prove all the strength of Jesus thine.
Commission'd angels soon shall come,
And waft thee to thy wish'd for home.

Joint heirs with Christ the Blessed,
The Father’s only Son,
So lifted into equal place
With that beloved One,

Before the Father’s face,

By heav’n’s most royal grace.

author: Richards, George, 1755?-1814
verses:

Of wrong, intended Joseph's blood,
His trembling brethren sue for peace,
And dread chastisement's iron rod.

Though evil they—yet Joseph good,
Comforts, speaks kind, wipes off their tears,
And standing as the type of God,
Removes each doubt—and calms all fears.

Thus does the soul of sinful men,
Heap indignation, anguish, wrath;
Till heav'n's own purpose in the plan,
Gleams mercy round his clouded path.

Lord, thou art good—supremely good!
No condemnation comes from thee:
When enemies redeem'd by blood;
Much more, thy life shall set us free.

title: Joseph made known to his brethren
author: Newton, John, 1725-1807
verses:
When Joseph his brethren beheld,
Afflicted and trembling with fear
His heart with compassion was fill'd,
From weeping he could not forbear:
A while his behaviour was rough;
to bring their past sins to their minds;
But when they were humbled enough,
He hasted to shew himself kind.

How little they thought it was he,
Whom they had ill-treated and sold!
How great their confusion must be,
As soon as his name he had told!
"I am Joseph your brother, he said,
And still to my heart you are dear,
You sold me, and thought i was dead,
But God for your sakes sent me here."

Tho' greatly distressed before,
When charg'd with purloining the cup
They now were confounded much more,
Not one of them durst to look up.
"Can Joseph, whom we would have slain
Forgive us the evil we did?
And will he our housholds maintain!
O this is a brother indeed"!

Thus dragg'd by my conscience I came,
And laden with guilt, to the Lord:
Surrounded with terror and shame,
Unable to utter a word.
At first he look'd stern and severe,
What anguish then pierced my heart
Expecting each moment to hear,
The sentence, "Thou cursed depart."

But oh! what surprise when he spoke,
While tenderness beam'd in his face:
My heart then to pieces was broke
O'erwhelm'd and counfounded by grace
Poor sinner I know thee full well,
By thee I was sold and was slain;
But I dy'd to redeem thee from hell,
And raise thee in glory to reign.

I am Jesus whom thou hast blasphem'd,
And crucify'd often afresh;
But let me henceforth be esteem'd
Thy brother, thy bone, and thy flesh
My pardon I freely bestow,
Thy wants I will fully supply;
I'll guide thee and guard thee below,
And soon will remove thee on high.

Go, publish to sinners around,
That they may be willing to come,
The mercy which now you have found
And tell them that yet there is room.
Oh, sinners, the message obey!
No more vain excuses pretend;
But come without further delay,
To JESUS, our brother, and friend.

title: Journeying Home
author: Davison, A. L., Mrs.
verses:
Thro' the years of the earthlife we journey,
And we sing as we pass along;
While the love that has saved and kept us,
Is the burden of our song.

In the Heaven of light and beauty,
Where the sunshine shall ne'er grow dim;
Where the night cometh never in darkness,
He will smile on us coming to him.

Ev'ry year in that world of glory,
Those we love find a hope of peace;
When our journey on earth is ended,
Shall the grief of our parting cease.

And the meeting beyond the river,
With the friends who have gone before;
Oh, what language can tell its blessing,
When we join them to part no more.
chorus:
O blessed Jesus, blessed Jesus,
The loving Savior of the world;
Thou hast conquered the grave,
Thou hast power to save,
And our souls find their hope in thee.

title: Journeying Homeward
author: Servoss, M. E. (Mary Elizabeth) 1849-1906

Journeying homeward, we joyously sing,
Eyes looking upward like daisies of spring,
Hearts full of gladness and earnest love,

What tho’ our friends pass away with the hour?
Storms never enter the pearly gates;
Jesus with friendship eternal awaits.

Bravely each trial we strive to bear,
Knowing the glory awaiting us there.

title: Journeying with Jesus
author: Bell, Birdie
verses:
Journeying with Jesus, in His chosen way,
Foll'wing in His footsteps we can never stray;
Sometimes on the mountain, sometimes in the vale,
Onward, ever trusting love which cannot fail.

Journeying with Jesus, in the heart a song,
Never in His presence can the road seem long;
Listening to His counsel, tender, kind, and true,
Keeping near the Master all the journey through.

Journeying with Jesus, all along the way,
Sorrows are forgotten, night is turned to day;
Resting on the promise, leaning on His arm,
Precious peace our portion, for we fear no harm.

Journeying with Jesus till the road shall end,
Faithful is our Leader, trusty is our Friend;
Asking for His guidance on our homeward way,
Till we lose the shadows, find eternal day.
chorus:
Journeying with Jesus, ever near His side,
Walking in the pathway where our Lord doth guide;
Singing as we travel to our home above,
Trusting in His mercy, resting in His love.

title: Joy and Praise
author: Cleator, Alice Jean, 1871-1926
verses:
There’s a song of gladness in the summer-land,
Summer land, summer land,
There’s a smile of welcome from the blossom band,
Blossom band, blossom band.
Let us in the joy unite,
‘Neath the summer’s golden light;
While the world is fair and bright,
Let us join the rapture of the summer-land.

O there’s sunlight falling down in golden show’rs,
Golden show’rs, golden show’rs,
Ev’ry bush and tree is garlanded with flow’rs,
Brightest flow’rs, brightest flow’rs.
Joy is in the perfumed air,
Life is reigning ev’rywhere;
Earth a bridal robe doth wear,
In the splendor of the summer’s happy ours.

There’s a message unto bird and blossom giv’n,
Blossom giv’n, blossom giv’n,
All are telling of the mighty pow’r of heav’n,
Pow’r of heav’n, pow’r of heav’n.
On this queen of summer days,
Let our hearts in loving praise,
Unto God their tribute raise,
Let us sound the glories of the King of heav’n.
chorus:
Joy and praise, joy and praise,
Ring in nature’s anthems sweet;
Joy and praise, joy and praise,
May each heart the strains repeat.

title: Joy and Sunshine
author: Marsh, Mary F.
verses:
Jesus is my joy and sunshine,
All along life’s dreary way;
His blest presence makes my pathway
Bright as heaven’s golden day.

And the glory of His presence
Fills my weary soul with peace;
And my heart is full of gladness—
Full of songs that never cease.

Day by day the way grows brighter;
O’er my path heav’n’s golden ray
Sheds its beams of glorious sunlight,
Like unto the “perfect day.”

Beauties never seen by mortals,
To the eye of faith appears;
As we near the heav’nly portals,
Far beyond this vale of tears.
chorus:

Peace, blessed peace is ever mine,

title: Joy, behold the Saviour
author: Whittle, D. W. (Daniel Webster), 1840-1901
verses:
Fierce and wild the storm is raging
Round a helpless bark,
On to doom 'tis swiftly driving
O'er the waters dark!

Weary, helpless, hopeless seamen,
Fainting on the deck,
With what joy they hail their Saviour,
As he hails the wreck!

On a wild and stormy ocean,
Sinking neath the wave,
Souls that perish heed the message,
Christ has come to save!

Daring death thy soul to rescue,
He in love has come;
Leave the wreck, and in him trusting,
Thou shalt reach thy home!

title: Joy-Bells
author: Pollard, Josephine, 1834-1892
verses:
Joy-bells ringing,
Children singing,
Fill the air with music sweet;
Joyful measure,
Guileless pleasure,
Make the chain of song complete.

Joy-bells ringing,
Children singing,
Hark! Their voices, loud and clear,
Breaking o’er us,
Like a chorus
From a purer, happier sphere.

Earth seems brighter,
Hearts grow lighter,
As the tuneful melody
Charms our sadness
Into gladness,
Pealing, pealing joyfully.

Joy-bells nearer
Sound, and clearer,
When the heart is free from care;
Skies are clearing,
While we’re hearing
Joy-bells ringing everywhere.
chorus:
Joy-bells! Joy-bells!
Never, never cease your singing;
List, list, the song that swells.
Joy-bells! Joy-bells!

title: Joy Bells
author: Crosby, Fanny, 1820-1915
verses:
Pretty, golden sunbeams,
Looking from the sky,
Call us now to wake and sing
Praise to God on high;
Song and beauty ev’rywhere,
On the earth and in the air,
Still the blessed truth declare,
God, our God, is love.

Pretty birds that carol
From the waving trees,
Hiding in the branches green,
Cradled on the breeze,
Through the laughing summer days
Still their great Creator praise;
In the simple tones they raise
Telling God is love.

Shall our tongues be silent?
Have we naught to say,
When our hearts can feel his love
Better far than they?
Like the beams that sparkle bright,
Like the birds on pinions light,
Like the bells, let all unite,
Singing, God is love.

Weeping for a night endures;
Joy the morning light ensures.

God’s own counsel standeth sure,
Ev’ry day of fortune’s frown
Hastens joy with robe and crown.

Speeds the hour when tears and pain
I can never know again,
Trustful, to this truth I cling;
Raptured, I this grace shall sing.

Joy the morning light ensures.

Blessed words of comfort in a time of grief,
“Joy will surely come when morning breaks,”
Strength and faith they carry, and a sweet relief,
Courage till the day awakes.

Dark may be the road on which our feet must tread,
Closed and sealed the door at which we wait,
Yet the light is ever shining overhead,
Angel hands unlock the gate.

From the blessed promise and its glory bright,
Ev’ry burdened heart new comfort takes,
Sorrow may endure throughout the weary night,
Joy will come when morning breaks.

author: Spring, George H.

Earth at times to us appears,
As a gloomy vale of tears,
But this thought the Christian cheers.
Joy cometh in the morning,
Sorrow always will be found
Where the fruits of sin abound:
Tho' this balm may work its wound,
Joy cometh in the morning.

Still 'tis well to learn below,
Whence originates our woe,
Only this at length we'll known 
Joy cometh in the morning,
Sin forsaking let us bear,
Patiently each grief and care,
Till we wake with Jesus, where
Joy cometh in the morning.

title: Joy Enough for Me
author: Rowe, James, 1865-1933
verses:
To share another’s trouble,
Whatever it may be,
And make his pathway brighter,
Is joy enough for me.

To cheer the sad and lonely,
To lessen misery
By word or smile or handclasp,
Is joy enough for me.

To help my fallen brother
A better man to be,
To help him onward, upward,
Is joy enough for me.

To help my Savior daily
The world from son to free,
To see him smile upon me,
Is joy enough for me.

No sweeter sound than this is heard,
Emmanuel!

Low at the cradle throne we bend,

Has come on earth to dwell;

Emmanuel!

Before the manger shrine,

We see Thee, Babe divine.
Rejoice, rejoice! Th'incarnate Word
Has come on earth to dwell;
No sweeter sound than this is heard,
Emmanuel!

Thou Light of uncreated Light,
Shine on us, Holy Child;
That we may keep Thy birthday bright,
With service undefiled.
Rejoice, rejoice! Th'incarnate Word
Has come on earth to dwell;
No sweeter sound than this is heard,
Emmanuel!

title: Joy fills the dwelling of the just
verses:
Joy fills the dwelling of the just,
Whom God has saved from harm;
For wondrous things are brought to pass
By His Almighty arm.

Then open wide the temple gates
To which the just repair,
That I may enter in, and praise
My great Deliverer there.

That which the builders once refused,
Is now the Corner-stone:
This is the wondrous work of God,
The work of God alone.

This day is god's; let all the lands
Exalt their cheerful voice:
"Lord, we beseech Thee, save us now,
And make us still rejoice."

O then with me give thanks to God,
who still does gracious prove;
And let the tribute of our praise
Be endless as His love.

title: Joy for Me

When my work is done and the vict’ry won,
When I come to the end of my way,
There is joy for me through eternity
In the land of endless day.

When the day shall break and I shall awake,
When my Savior in glory I see;
I will offer praise, glad hosannas raise
For His wondrous love to me.

In a glad new song with the ransomed throng
Where there never shall come any night,
I shall sing God’s praise through unending days,
In the mansions of delight.

Those who left us here ‘mid our flowing tear,
We shall meet on the bright, golden shore;
All bereavement past, we shall meet at last,
Reunited evermore.

title: Joy in the HOLY GHOST
author: Mason, John, 1646?-1694
verses:
My Soul doth magnify the Lord,
My Spirit doth rejoice
In God my Saviour and my God,
I hear his joyful Voice.

I need not go abroad for Joy
Who have a Feast at home;
My Sighs are turned into Songs,
The Comforter is come.

Down from Above the blessed Dove
Is come into my Breast,
To Witness God's eternal Love;
This is my heavenly Feast.

This makes me Abba, Father, cry,
With Confidence of Soul;
It makes me cry, My Lord, my God,
And that without controul.

There is a Stream which issues forth
From god's eternal Throne,
And from the Lamb, a living Stream,
Clear as the Crystal Stone.

The Streams doth Water Paradise,
It makes the Angels sing:
One cordial Drop revives my Heart;
Hence all my Joys do spring.

Such Joys as are unspeakable,
And full of Glory too;
Such hidden Manna, hidden Pearls,
As Worldlings do not know.

Eye hath not seen, nor Ear hath heard,
From Fancy 'tis conceal'd,
What thou, Lord, hast laid up for thine,
And hast to me reveal'd.

I see thy Face, I hear thy Voice,
I taste thy sweetest Love;
My Soul doth Leap: but O for Wings,
The Wings of Noah's Dove!

Then should I flee far hence away,
Leaving this World of Sin:
Then Would my Lord put forth his Hand
And kindly take me in.

Then would my Soul with Angels feast
On Joys that always last:
Blest be my God, the God of Joy,
Who gives me here a Taste.

title: Joy is a Fruit that will not grow
author: Newton, John, 1725-1807
verses:
Joy is a Fruit that will not grow
In Nature's barren Soil;
All we can boast, 'till Christ we know,
Is Vanity and Toil.

But where the Lord has planted Grace,
And made his Glories known;
There Fruits of Heav'nly Joy and Peace
Are found, and there alone.

A bleeding Saviour, seen by Faith,
A Sense of Pard'ning Love,
A Hope that triumphs over Death,
Give Joys like those above.

To make a Glimpse within the Vail,
To know that God is mine;
Are Springs of Joy that never fail,
Unspeakably Divine.

These are the Joys that satisfy,
And sanctify the Mind;
Which make the spirit mount on High,
And leave the World behind.

No more Believers, mourn your Lot,
But if you are the Lord's,
Resign to them that know him not,
Such Joys as Earth affords.

title: Joy Is Coming In the Morning
author: Wilson, Jennie, 1857-1913

Tho' the soul grow faint and weary
‘Mid the sadness of the night,
Soon upon the darkness dreary
There will glow a blessed light;
And the gladness of that dawning
Will all tears of grief repay,
Joy is coming in the morning,
When the shadows flee away.

Thro' the hours of bitter weeping,
When thou seemest all alone,
God a tender watch is keeping,
Every sigh to him is known;
After all the anxious waking,
After all the fitful dreams,
Joy is coming with the breaking
Of the morning’s golden beams.

Thro the time of pain and sorrow
Trust the love and care divine,
Wait the radiant tomorrow,
Soon its blessing shall be thine;
God’s unceasing guard is o’er thee,
And the gloom will soon be gone,
Joy is coming with the glory
Of a holy, cloudless dawn.
chorus:

author: Harkness, Robert, 1880-1961

title: Joyful, Joyful, We Adore Thee
author: Henry J. van Dyke
verses: Joyful, joyful, we adore Thee, God of glory, Lord of love; Hearts unfold like flowers before Thee, opening to the sun above. Melt the clouds of sin and sadness; drive the dark of doubt away; Giver of immortal gladness, fill us with the light of day!

All Thy works with joy surround Thee, earth and heaven reflect Thy rays, Stars and angels sing around Thee, center of unbroken praise. Field and forest, vale and mountain, flowery meadow, flashing sea, Singing bird and flowing fountain call us to rejoice in Thee.

Thou art giving and forgiving, ever blessing, ever blessed, Wellspring of the joy of living, ocean depth of happy rest! Thou our Father, Christ our Brother, all who live in love are Thine; Teach us how to love each other, lift us to the joy divine.

Mortals, join the happy chorus, which the morning stars began; Father love is reigning o'er us, brother love binds man to man. Ever singing, march we onward, victors in the midst of strife, Joyful music leads us Sunward in the triumph song of life.

title: Joyful Praise

When the morning breaks in splendor
O'er the valley, warm and tender,
Joyful praise our hearts would render
To our Father God on high;
Thro' the night, when all were sleeping,
We were guarded safe beneath his care,
When the stars their watch were keeping
In the calm, blue sky so fair.

When the noontide hour is beaming,
Happy songs each bird is singing,
May our hearts in measure ringing,
Praise our Father God on high;
With a gentle hand he leads us,
He is still our patient, loving Friend,
And the hand we now are holding
Will protect us to the end.

When the evening winds are sighing,
And the light is softly dying,
Then, to nature's voice replying
Praise our Father on high;
He has crowned our life with mercy,
He has scattered blessings on our way,
And we hope to see and praise him
In the realms of endless day.

He bestows from above!
Let our souls and all within us
Praise the Lord for all his love.

Joyfully, joyfully haste to thy home.

Oh, joyous, joyous Easter day,
Oh, blessed, blessed feast,
When Jesus Christ, our risen Lord,
Becomes our great High Priest.
His body broken feeds our souls,
And blessed life imparts;
His blood, a sacred wine, poured forth,
Renews our fainting hearts.

Oh, joyous, joyous Easter day,
For Christ our risen Lord,
Has conquered death and pow’rs of hell,
By His own spoken word;
And Paradise is opened wide
For all to enter in,

Redeems from death and sin.

For death has now no sting,
The grave has lost its victory
Through Jesus Christ our King.

Through our Redeemer’s grace.

Soft o'er the fountain,
Ling'ring falls the southern moon;
Far o'er the mountain
Breaks the day too soon!
In thy dark eyes' splendor,
Where the warm light loves to dwell,
Weary looks, yet tender,
Speak their fond farewell,
Nita! Juanita!
Ask thy soul if we should part!
Nita! Juanita!
Lean thou on my heart.

When in thy dreaming
Moons like these shall shine again,
And daylight beaming
Prove thy dreams are vain,
Wilt thou not, relenting,
For thine absent lover sigh?
In thy heart consenting
To a pray'r gone by?
Nita! Juanita!
Let me linger by thy side!
Nita Juanita!
Be my own fair bride.

How jubilant and clear they ring
Those joyous Easter bells,
As to and fro their great tongues swing
How sweet their music swells,
The gentle breezes catch the tones,
And waft them far and near,
Of hope and comfort do they speak
Unto the list’ning ear.

How cheerily and blithe they ring
Those gladsome Easter bells,
As to and fro their great tongues swing
Of love their music tells.
The Father sent His only Son
From realms of bliss on high,
Upon the Mount of Calvary 
For sinful men to die.

How merrily and gaily ring
Those happy Easter bells,
As to and fro their great tongues swing
How clear their music sells.
The grave could not enchain our King,
Death must yield up its prey,
The Victor over every foe,
Christ Jesus rose today.

With joyful hearts we hail the day
That finds us tracing all our way;
That bids us lift our eyes and see
The love that crowns our Jubilee.

The faithful servants of the Lord,
Who now from all their toil are free,

This year of my jubilee, ye shall return.

title: Judge thou my Cause, O GOD!
author: Hopkinson, Francis, 1737-1791
verses:
Judge thou my Cause, O GOD!
For I have ever trod
The Paths that righteous are and just;
I shall not be disgraced,
Since I have always placed,
In thee alone my Hope and Trust

Search, prove each inward Part;
Examine thou my Heart
Which lies uncover'd to thy View:
From Sin I have refrained,
My Righteousness retained,
And will the Ways of Truth pursue.

For still I keep thy Grace,
O LORD, before my Face,
And in thy Mercy take Delight;
Thy Truth is my Direction,
To bring me to Perfection,
And keep me in the Path that's right.

The Idle or Profane,
Could ne'er my Friendship gain;
For in their Deeds I take not Part:
Nor could the sly Deceiver,
With all his Treach'ry, ever
Win to his Ways my faithful Heart.

I hat the busy Crew,
Who Mischief still pursue,
And ever make distracted Times;
Their Ways I ne'er approved,
Their Converse never loved,
But shun them as I shun their Crimes.
Part II

My Hands in Innocence,
I'll wash from all Offence;
Make thou, Oh GOD, my Heart so pure,
That to thy Altar going,
No Spot or Blemish shewing,
My Welcome may be found secure.

My Thanks I'll publish there,
And to the World declare,
Thy vast Renown and mighty Fame;
My Heart with Rapture glowing,
My Tongue for ever shwoing,
The Honours due to thy great Name.

Urg'd by a wicked spite,
They seize another's Right,
And make Oppression thus their Trade;
They secret Bribes are taking,
Their Oaths in private breaking,
Or else by open Force invade.

My Foes assail in vain,
I still my Ground maintain;
Tho' arm'd with Rage they stand around:
Among the Congregation
Of Saints, I'll fix my Station,
Thy Praises ever to resound.

title: Judgment
verses:
Hark! ye Mortals, hear the Trumpet,
Sounding loud the mighty Roar;
Hark! th' Arch-Angel's Voice proclaiming,
Thou old Time, shalt be no more.
Rolling Ages, rolling Ages, rolling Ages,
Now your solemn close appears.

This great rolling Frame of nature,
That huge Mass of blazing Day,
Yonder arch'd expance of Heav'n,
Ye must all dissoolve away.
Hark! th' Arch-Angel, Hark! th' Arch-Angel, Hark! th' Arch-Angel,
Swells the solemn summons loud.

See the gloomy Prisoners rising,
Hell's dark caverns gaping wide;
Wild Confusion sieze the Christless,
Horrors fill the spacious void:
Come ye Mountains, come ye Mountains, come ye Mountains,
Hide us from this dire Revenge.

See the purple Banner flying,
Hear the Judgment-Chariot roll;
Hear the Saviour's Words of mercy:
Come, ye ransom'd Heav'n-born Souls.
Judge these Nations, judge these Nations, judge these Nations,
Now they all shall feel my Pow'r.

Hurl'd in countless Numbers downward,
See in wild disorder driv'n;
Tortur'd with Despair and Anguish,
Left (and that for ever) Heav'n,
How Tremendous, how Tremendous, how Tremendous,
Sounds their last decisive Doom.

See the Souls that Earth dispised,
In celestial Glories move;
Hallelujah's big with wonder
Praising Christ's eternal Love:
Hallelujahs, Hallelujahs, Hallelujahs,
Echo through the Realms of Light.

Joys ecstatic, Hymns harmonious,
In soft Symphony resound,
Angels, Seraphs, Harps, and Trumpets,
Swell the sweet Angelic Sound:
Hail! Almighty! Hail! Almighty! Hail! Almighty!
Great eternal Lord, Amen.

title: Judgment
verses:
He comes! he comes! the trumpet sound
And loudly rend the vast profound;
Earth, sea, and sky astonish'd shake:
To judgment come--ye dead awake!

Behold, behold what myriads rise!
See! see what glory fills the skies:
The dreadful volumes open shine;
O! mercy, Lord--for mercy's thine.

The hour, the awful hour is come,
Fix'd, ever fix'd is human doom;
The earth dissolves, heav'n melts away:
O shield me, Saviour, in that day.

Lo! he ascends, to heaven ascends,
With his triumphant right-hand friends:
Time, death, and hell, expiring lye,
And goodness fills eternity.

The Father bless--the Son adore,
The Spirit praise for evermore:
Salvation's glorious work is done:
We welcome thee, great Three One.

title: Judgment
verses:
Press'd my soul with future prospect,
Sing creation's dismal end;
Long foretold by sacred Prophets,
Holy Muse thy succours lend.
Say what horror what confusion,
Will each sinful heart dismay
What distresses, tortures, anguish
Reign in that tremendous day.

Rumbling Thunders forky shinings,
Ghastly glaring thwart the gloom;
Nature shaking to her center,
Groans prophetic of her doom.
Cliffy rocks and lofty mountains,
O'er the trembling basis rock;
While Earth yawns in dreaful chasme,
With the each strong repeated shock.

Seas with horrid palpitation,
Ravage round their frighted shores,
Blustering wind with frantic fury,
Through each ruin'd fabric roars,
The Suns' bright orb is veil'd in sackcloth
Stripp'd of all his sparkling beams;
The moon has dropp'd her silver radiance
And dissolves in purple streams.

Stars of light divinely brilliant,
Studding night, Cimmerian robe;
Hurl'd in darkness from their orbits,
Each a darken'd ruin'd globe.
Hark! the martial trumpet sounding
Rends in twain the crystal sky;
Vengeance blazing lights the concave
Of profound eternity.

See the sovereign Aether furling;
Nobler scenes salute mine eyes;
Heav'n in solemn pomp descending,
Crimson banners dress the skies.
On the arched striped rainbow,
Sits entrhon'd the eteranl God,
Myriads of Celestial Warriors
Round him wait his awful nod.

Go, he grieves, ye winged herald,
Bring my saints from ev'ry wind,
Those my blood from death has ransom'd
Those in life's fair volume penn'd,
Strait a holy troop obsequious,
Swift as lightning skim'd along,
And from ev'ry grave collecting,
Jesus' dear redeemed Throng.

Death no more with livid aspect,
Spurs his sallow steed to stay;
Now the ravenous foe disgorges,
All his long imprison'd prey,
Rous'd from Tombs each wicked rises,
By the trumpet's thrilling sound
Round they stare with wild amazement,
Wond'ring at the scene profound.

Fill'd with horror dread and anguish,
Rocks and mountains they implore,
To fall and crush them out of being;
Wishing now to be no more.
Hark the Herald calls to judgment,
Justice draws her glittering sword,
Lightning glances from his aspect;
Thunder clothe his awful word.

Go ye cursed fill'd with vengeance,
Nor for peace my name invoke;
Ye who once despis'd my mercy,
And my fury dare provoke:
Go to pits of burning sulphur,
Ever banish'd from my rest,
Where the souls eternal larum,
Ceaseless beats your pulsive breast.

title: Judgment
author: Addison, Joseph, 1672-1719
verses:
When rising from the Bed of Death,
O’erwhelmed with Guilt and Fear,
I view my Maker Face to Face
O how shall I appear.

If yet, while Pardon may be found,
And Mercy may be sought,
My soul with inward Horror shrinks,
and trembles at the Thought;

When thou o Lord shalt stand disclos'd
In Majesty severe,
And sit in Judgment on my soul,
O how shall I appear!

O may my broken, contrite Heart
Timely my Sins lament,
And early with repentant Tears
Eternal Woe prevent!

Behold the Sorrows of my Heart,
E'er yet it be too late;
And hear my Saviour’s dying Groans,
to give those sorrows weight.

For never shall my soul despair
Her Pardon to secure;
Who knows the only Son has died
To make that Pardon sure.

title: June Song
author: Cleator, Alice Jean, 1871-1926

In the dim woodlands,
Silent and deep,
Blossoms are waking,
From their long sleep.
Bird songs are ringing
On every hand,
Blue skies are smiling,
O’er a fair land.

Out in the meadows, 
Gay brooklets run,
Shining like silver,
In the bright sun.
Mountains are smiling,
In robes of green,
O’er all the landscape,
Beauty is seen.

Trees of the woodland,
Birds of the air,
Splendor of sunset,
All are most fair.
Then let our praises 
Rise unto heav’n,
For all this beauty,
So freely giv’n.
chorus:

At the fairest season of the year,
Let none be sad,
Let all be glad
For the golden summer time is here.

For my strength is small, and insufficient too;

Just a little helper for Jesus anywhere,

title: "Just a Little Longer"
author: Morris, C. H., Mrs. 1862-1929
verses:
Just a little longer to work for Jesus,
Days for earthly toil are short and few;
Just a little longer to fight life's battles,
And to prove thyself a soldier brave and true.

Just a little longer the seed to scatter
Out upon the harvest-fields so wide;
Just a little longer the sheaves to gather,
Coming with rejoicing at the eventide.

Just a little longer to lift the fallen,
Precious, never-dying souls to save;
Just a little longer to tell the story,
And to speed the message o'er the ocean wave.
chorus:
Just a little longer, just a little longer,
O my soul be patient, to the end endure;
Just a little longer the cross to bear,
Then a long eternity the crown to wear.

title: Just a Little Nearer
author: Fyke, C. A.
verses:
Heav'nly Father, I would be
Just a little nearer;
I would all thy glory see
Just a little clearer.

Lest I wander, Lord, from thee,
Just a little nearer
May thy Spirit ever be
Just a little nearer.

Let thy love encompass me,
Just a little nearer;
Height and depth of love must be
Just a little nearer.
chorus:
Nearer, nearer would I be,
Just a little nearer;
Draw me nearer, Lord, to thee,
Just a little nearer.

title: Just a Little While
author: Chisholm, Thomas O. 1866-1960
verses:
Just a little while and the day will dawn,
And the dreary night, be forever gone;
Just a little while e’er the storms will cease,
Ere the heav’nly calm the eternal peace.

Just a little while, then, the toils all done,
And the battle fought, and the vict’ry won,
We shall lay the cross and the burden down,
To receive at last heaven’s promised crown.

Just a little while and the tears that stray
Down our faces now, God will wipe away;
And the bitter pain and the wand’rings lone
All will surely end at the Father’s throne.

Just a little while—let us work and wait,
Till our Father’s hand opens wide the gate,
And we hear his voice sweetly bid us come,
Evermore to dwell with the Lord at home.
chorus:
Just a little while, O it won’t be long,
Courage, fainting heart! let your faith be strong;
Soon our weary feet to the end will come—
Glory be to God! we are almost home.

title: Just a Little While
author: McCauley, W. F. (William Fletcher), 1858-
verses:
Oh, my Savior bids me wait a little while,
And the dawning of the morning I shall see!
He will greet me with a kind and loving smile,
When I reach the home in heav’n prepared for me.

I shall patiently abide this little while!
Learning love’s enduring lesson while I wait,
Yielding not to earthly pleasures that beguile,
Waiting for the op’ening of the golden gate.

Father, help me work and pray this little while,
In the service finding gladness day by day,
Turning others from temptations that defile,
Winning souls to walk with joy the heav’nly way.

Oh, the blessings that surround this little while
Are a foretaste of his glory for my soul;
Thro’ the clouds I see the sunlight of his smile,
Soon will billows of salvation o’er me roll!
chorus:
Just a little while!
Just a little while!
Till the dawning of the morning bright and fair!
Just a little while!
Just a little while!
I shall meet him with the angles in the air.

title: Just a Little While
author: Bartlett, E. M. (Eugene Monroe). 1885-1941
verses:
Soon this life will all be over
And our pilgrimage will end,
Soon we’ll take our heav’nly journey,
Be at home again with friends;
Heaven’s gates are standing open,
Waiting for our entrance there,
Some sweet day we’re going over,
All the beauties there to share.

Soon we’ll see the light of morning,
Then the new day will begin,
Soon we’ll hear the Father calling,
“Come, my children enter in;”
Then we’ll hear a choir of angels,
Singing out the vict’ry song,
All our troubles will be ended
And we’ll live with heaven’s throng.

Soon we’ll meet again our loved ones
And we’ll take them by the hand,
Soon we’ll press them to our bosom
Over in the promised land;
Then we’ll be at home forever,
Thro’out all eternity,
What a blessed, blessed morning
That eternal morn will be!
chorus:
Just a little while to stay here,
Just a little while to wait;
Just a little while to labor
In the path that’s always straight;
Just a little more of troubles
In this low and sinful state,
Then we’ll enter heaven’s portals,
Sweeping thro’ the pearly gates.

We shall walk life’s thorny ways,

title: Just a Ray of Sunshine
author: Blenkhorn, Ada, 1858–1927
verses:
Just a ray of sunshine
Breaking thro' the gloom,
Makes the earth rejoice again,
And the flow'rs to bloom:
Makes the earth rejoice again
And makes the flow'rs to bloom.

Just a little kindness,
Bright and sunny smile,
Makes the sad heart sing again,
All its cares beguile,
Makes the sad heart sing again
And all its cares beguile.

Words and smiles so kindly
Like the sunshine fall,
Let your presence ever be
Blessings unto all;
Let your presence ever be
Rich blessings unto all.

title: Just a Step to Jesus
author: Tubbs, Arthur Lewis, 1867-1946
verses:
It is just a step to Jesus;
Will you take it, friend, tonight?
While He waiteth to receive you,
Won’t you enter into light?
With a love so deep and tender,
Deeper than the deepest sea,
He implores you and invites you,
Kindly saying, “Come to me.”

It is just a step to Jesus;
Haste, O haste, and take it now!
Breathe a pray’r, for He is list’ning,
Make to Him a solemn vow;
Place your hand in His confiding,
Let Him lead you where He will,
Thro’ the meadows green with verdure,
By the waters cool and still.

It is just a step to Jesus;
Sinner, won’t you cross the line?
Won’t you let His grace, so precious,
In your life forever shine?
Tho’ the world has charms, alluring,
They are like the fading leaf,
And at last will fall and wither,—
Leaving only pain and grief.

It is just a step to Jesus;
Do not tarry, come tonight!
Look to Him, and He will lead you
Out of darkness into light;
With a full and glad surrender
Put your trust in Him, and say,
“Where Thou leadest, O my Saviour,
I will follow all the way.?

title: Just A Sunbeam
author: Payn, A. A. (see also Charles Austin Miles)
verses:
Just a sunbeam shining from above,
On a golden morning,
Touch'd a blossom with a ray of love
And death was changed to life.
O the pow'r of love,
Wondrous pow'r of love,
Easing pain and woe;
O that all may be,
Sunbeams light and free 
Ev'rywhere we go.

Just a sunbeam, but its cheering ray,
Lightens ev'ry burden;
Weary travellers on the upward way
Are cheer'd and helped and bless'd.
O the pow'r of love,
Wondrous pow'r of love,
Easing pain and woe;
O that all may be, 
Sunbeams light and free
Ev'rywhere we go.

Just a sunbeam, but a welcome guest;
In some darken'd dwelling
One may enter, with its message blest,
And with its light of love.
O the pow'r of love,
Wondrous pow'r of love,
Easing pain and woe;
O that all may be,
Sunbeams light and free 
Ev'rywhere we go.

But a sunbeam, smiling as you go,
Bearing golden blessings
Into homes and lives of want or woe,
O carry love's bright ray.
O the pow'r of love,
Wondrous pow'r of love,
Easing pain and woe;
O that all may be,
Sunbeams light and free 
Ev'rywhere we go.
chorus:
Shine, ever shine, O sunbeam bright,
Turn winter's darkness into light,
Emblem thou, of heav'n's bright morning,
Foll'wing earth's night.

title: Just a Touch of Jesus
author: Cassel, E. T. (Elijah Taylor), 1849-1930

She only touched the hem of the garment that he wore;
Just a little touch in faith did perfect health restore.
The virtue of the Lord floweth free to ev’ry soul,
Who comes to him in simple faith to be made whole.

In gloom and want and darkness e’er longing for the day,
Thus the blind of Jericho sat begging by the way;
But Jesus passing by heard their eager, earnest cries,
And spoke the wondrous word that opened wide their eyes.

Oh, weary, burdened soul, to the Savior quickly go;
Tho’ your sins be scarlet, they shall be as white as snow,
Now go with all your sorrow, yes, go with all your sin,
For Jesus’ touch is life and joy and peace within.
chorus:
Just a touch of Jesus! Just a touch of Jesus!
Just a touch that makes the sinner whole;
Just a touch of Jesus! Just a touch of Jesus!
Just a little touch that saves the soul!

Now just a word for Jesus;
Your dearest Friend so true,
Come, cheer our hearts and tell us
What He has done for you.

Now just a word for Jesus;
You feel your sins forgiv'n,
And by His grace are striving
To reach a home in heav'n.

Now just a word for Jesus;
A cross it cannot be
To say, "I love my Saviour
Who gave His life for me"

Now just a word for Jesus;
And if your faith be dim,
Arise in all your weakness,
And leave the rest to Him.
chorus:
Now just a word for Jesus
'Twill help us on our way;
One little word for Jesus,
O speak, or sing, or pray.

title: Just a Word with Jesus
author: Morris, C. H., Mrs. 1862-1929

Just a word with Jesus
Before the day begins,
Just a plea for guidance
A day of blessing wins;
Just a moment’s waiting
In silence at his feet,
Just to hear him whisper
His words of counsel sweet.

Just a tho’t in secret,
A little whispered pray’r
Makes the heart courageous,
And lifts a load of care;
Just a glimpse of Jesus,
To faith’s unwav’ring sight,
Turns the clouds to sunshine,
And makes the whole day bright.

Just a word with Jesus—
But how much it means
When with trust unbroken
A soul upon him leans;
Grant, O precious Savior,
Tho’ much denied may be,
We, thro’ life’s short journey,
May walk and talk with thee.

Talk to Jesus often,
Heart to heart and face to face,

For what he’s done for you,
Talk to Jesus often,
This Friend so true.

title: Just Across the River
author: Herrick, S. B., Mrs.
verses:
Just across the river,
On the golden shore,
Where the crystal sunlight
Beams for ever more.
'Mid the heav'nly bowers,
'Mid the fadeless bloom,
Dwell the happy children,
In their blissful home.

Hark! the sound of voices,
'Tis the echo sweet,
Of the children singing
At the Saviour's feet;
'Tis the glorious anthem,—
Rising ever more,
Of the love that brought them
To that golden shore.

Jesus loves the children,
Who his praises sing;
Though they wear the earth-robe,
He is still their King:
He will gently guide them,
Till the night is o'er;
Then they'll join the chorus
On the golden shore.
chorus:
Would you cross the river,
To the golden shore,
Give your heart to Jesus,
He will guide you o'er.

title: Just Approach it With a Song
author: Bell, Birdie
verses:
When you come to snares and pitfalls,
When temptations round you throng;
Bravely meet each threat’ning danger,
Just approach it with a song.

Gladly take each joy that’s offer’d,
Ev’ry smile that comes along;
Then when grief stands in your pathway,
Just approach it with a song.

Trust in God, He’ll keep you ever,
He will help you conquer wrong;
Do not flinch at sight of danger,
Just approach it with a song.

Do not fear the tempter’s power,
Faint not, tho’ the road is long;
God will help you meet each peril,
Just approach it with a song.

Just approach it with a song.

title: Just as God Leads Me
author: Gedicke, Lampertus, 1683-1735
verses:
Just as God leads me, I would go,
I would not ask to choose my way;
Content with what he will bestow,
Assured he will not let me stray.
So as he leads, my path I make,
And step by step I gladly take,
A child in him confiding.

Just as God leads I am content,
I rest me calmly in his hands;
That which he has decreed and sent
That which his will for me commands.
I would that he should all fulfil,
That I should do his gracious will,
In living or in dying.

Just as God leads I all resign,
I trust me to my Father's will;
When reason's rays deceptive shine,
His counsel would I yet fulfil.
That which his love ordained as right
Before he bro't me to the light,
My all to him resigning.

"Just as I am," thine own to be,
Friend of the young, who lovest me:
To consecrate myself to thee,
O Jesus Christ, I come, I come.

In the glad morning of my day,
My life to give, my vows to pay,
With no reserve and no delay,
With all my heart I come, I come.

I would live ever in the light,
I would work ever for the right,
I would serve thee with all my might,
Therefore to thee I come, I come.

"Just as I am," young, strong and free,
To be the best that I can be
For truth, and righteousness, and thee,
Lord of my life, I come, I come.

Just as I am
Just as I am,
O Lord, I come.
Just as I am,
Just as I am
Just as I am,
O Lord, I come.

That Christ, my Saviour, cares for me,

And blessings rich on me bestows,

That where He is, there I may be,
Throughout a long eternity.

Just as I am, O Lamb of God,
Now I come, now I come;
To wash me in Thy cleansing blood,
Now I come, now I come.
While mercy’s guiding beacons beam
To point to the crimson stream

Now I come, now I come.

Now I come, now I come;
To Christ the true and living Way,
Now I come, now I come.

Now I come, now I come.

Just as I am, without one plea,
But that Thy blood was shed for me,
And that Thou bid'st me come to Thee,
O Lamb of God, I come!

Just as I am, and waiting not
To rid my soul of one dark blot,
To Thee, whose blood can cleanse each spot,
O Lamb of God, I come!

Just as I am, though tossed about
With many a conflict, many a doubt,
Fightings within, and fears without,
O Lamb of God, I come!

Just as I am--poor,wretched, blind,

Yea, all I need, in Thee to find,
O Lamb of God, I come!

Just as I am--Thou wilt receive,
Wilt welcome, pardon, cleanse, relieve;
Because Thy promise I believe,
O Lamb of God, I come!

Just as I am-- Thy love unknown
Hath broken every barrier down;
Now, to be Thine, yea, Thine alone,
O Lamb of God, I come!

Whose hand shall mark my path for me,

Just as my Father wills.

He chastens but to purify;
Just as my Father wills.

The God I trust the end can see;
In weal or woe my song shall be:—
Just as my Father wills.

author: Cook, Russell Sturgis, 1811-1864

Just as thou art--without one trace
Of love, or joy, or inward grace,
Or meetness for the heav'nly place,
O guilty sinner, come, O come.

Trust not the world, it gives no rest,
I bring relief to hearts opprest,
O weary sinner come, O come.

Count all thy gains but empty dross:
My grace repays all earthly loss--

O trembling sinner, come, O come.

title: Just Ask Him in to Stay
author: Farmer, Silas, 1839-1902
verses:
Our hearts are light and cheerful,
We're full of joy today;
The Savior is our welcome Guest--
We've asked Him in to stay.

Each day is full of gladness,
And ev'ry month is May;
The Savior is our helpful Friend--
We're asked Him in to stay.

Swinging every heart wide open,
For Christ, the Truth, the Way,
Is waiting with a blessing race--
Just ask Him in to stay.
chorus:
Just ask Him in to stay.
He'll brighten ev'ry day,
His grace is so abounding,
He'll drive all gloom away.

title: Just Because He Loved Me
author: Martin, Civilla D. (Civilla Durfee), 1866-1948
verses:
Jesus took me in, saved my soul from sin,
Just because, because He loved me;
Full atonement made, ev’ry debt He paid,
Because He loved me.

Came He down to die from His throne on high,
Just because, because He loved me;
Lived a lowly life, suffered care and strife,
Because He loved me.

By the world denied, suffered He and died,
Just because, because He loved me;
Victor He arose over all His foes,
Because He loved me.

He at Pentecost sent the Holy Ghost,
Just because, because He loved me;
Ever by my side will my Lord abide,
Because He loved me.

title: Just Beyond
author: Harris, E. Z., Mrs.
verses:
Just beyond life's weary labor,
Just beyond this world of care,
Lies a fair and wondrous city
Which the faithful all may share.
In that blest and happy country
Shall be heard no voice of woe
And we'll meet our sleeping loved ones,
"Loved and lost so long ago."

There the flow'rs are fadeless ever,
There the gentle breezes blow;
There we'll rest from toils and trials
Where life's waters softly flow.
Just beyond are crowns of glory,
Harps of gold and robes of white.
These are waiting for the faithful
Where there is no death nor night.

Burdened with earth's many sorrows
Oft I cry, "How long to wait
Till those glories be my portion?
When will open life's fair gate?"
Angel voices to me whisper,
"Soon will earth's dark night be o'er,
Soon will come earth's great Deliv'er,
Soon we'll rest on that blest shore."

Just beyond this weary way,
Just beyond, just beyond,
Riseth one unclouded day;

title: Just Beyond
author: Widmeyer, C. B. (Charles Brenton), 1884-1974
verses:
Just beyond the silent river, Where the sages weep no more:
Voices join in glad hosannas To the King for evermore.
Christ the conqueror from Bozrah, Garments dyed in crimson red,
Bought redemption for earth's aliens By His triumph from the dead.

No more weeping over yonder, There we'll say farewell no more:
Blessed bright and happy morning, When we meet on that blest shore:
Ages past, still ages coming, Yet no end will we know there,
Heaven beams with grandest splendor To all whom are free from care.

I am nearing now the crossing, Soon the boatman will row o'er:
He will pilot to the haven, There the Christ we will adore;
Saved from sin and strife forever, Safe in Jesus' fond embrace,
Dwelling with the hosts of angels, While we sing the "songs of grace."

title: Just Beyond the Hills of Time
author: Rowe, James, 1865-1933
verses:
There's a home for you, a home for me
In a fairer, better clime;
It is just across a narrow sea—
Just beyond the hills of time.

Christ, the sinner's friend, who saves by grace,
Now prepares that happy home;
There we all may meet Him face to face,
When on earth we cease to roam.

In that home of light our loved ones wait,
Pure as snow and fair as day;
They will meet us at the golden gate,
At the ending of the way.

Let us watch and pray and follow Him,
Sweetly singing through the gloam,
Till shall flee away the shadows dim,
And we all reach home, sweet home.
chorus:
Just beyond the hills of time,
Just across the narrow sea,
Where the angels raise ceaseless strains of praise,
There's a home for you and me.

Just beyond the pearly gates.

Just beyond the pearly gates;

Just beyond the pearly gates

Just beyond the pearly gates.

Just beyond the river.

title: Just Cling to the Word of God
author: Grinnell, O. S.
verses:
Amidst the cares and toils of life,
Just cling to the word of God,
If others falter in the strife,
Just cling to the word of God.
There is no book as good as this,
It shows the way of righteousness,
It opens wide the door of bliss,
Just cling to the word of God.

Just cling to the word of God,
Just cling to the word of God;
It opens wide the door of bliss,
Just cling to the word of God.

If friends forsake, they surely may,
Just cling to the word of God,
‘Twill guide you safely night and day,

The mind of God is there in wrought,

The way of life can there be sought,

The story old, yet ever new,
Just cling to the word of God.

Just cling to the word of God;
The story old, yet ever new,
Just cling to the word of God.

title: Just for His Sake
author: Henry, S. M. I. (Sarepta Myrenda Irish), 1839-1900
verses:
I have toiled all night and for many a day;
They say there are fish in the sea,
Yet I’ve caught nothing, my labor is vain,
There cometh no increase to me.
I will wash out my net, I will hang it away,
And my fishing boat draw to the shore,
It is useless to me, I will cast out my net
In these barren sea-waters no more.

And he bent o’er the labor of washing his net,
While Jesus walked down to the sea,
And entered the ship at the mooring and said,
“Thrust the boat out a little for me.
Launch out into the deep, and let down the net,”
And the fisherman answer’d, “In vain
We have labored all night, and yet at thy word
I will cast in my net once again.”

And how it was done the Lord only knows,
But the net was so filled that it brake;
For they launched out the ship and they cast in the net,
At the Master’s word, just for his sake.
And so, tho’ thy labor is vain until now,
Lo, Jesus is saying to thee:
“Launch out into the deep now and cast in the net,
There are fish in the depths of the sea.”

title: Just for Jesus Sake
author: Gabriel, Chas. H. (Charles Hutchinson), 1856-1932
verses:
Are you heavy hearted, and oppressed with grief and care,
Weary of the duty-burden you in silence bear?
Faithful be, and patient—never yielding to despair,
Bear it, bravely bear it, just for Jesus’ sake.

Do you long for pleasures that allure on ev’ry side?
Think of Him—the Man of Sorrows—by His own denied!
Count it joy to suffer in His name, however tried,
Bear it, bravely bear it, just for Jesus’ sake.

When temptation whispers “’Tis for other hands to do!”
Think what He endured in dark Gethsemane for you;
Take the cross He gives you! to the blessed One be true,
Bear it, bravely bear it, just for Jesus’ sake.
chorus:
Be a christian brave and true;
Bear the cross He gives to you:
Heavy tho’ it prove, yet in faith and love,
Bravely bear it just for Jesus’ sake.

title: Just for To-day
author: De Armond, Lizzie, 1847-1936
verses:
Just for today, dear Father, we pray,
Bright let Thy love-light gleam o’er our way;
Wash us and make our hearts pure within,
Take from us e’en the longing to sin.

Just for today, oh, help us to be
Lights trimmed and burning, shining for Thee;
Where duty calls us, pointing the way,
Serving Thee truly each passing day.

Just for today, whatever betide,
Clasp our hands closer, walk by our side;
Safe in Thy keeping, naught can affright,
Following Jesus, darkness is light.
chorus:
Just for today,
Just for today,
Guide us and keep us
Just for today.

title: Just for To-Day
author: Rexford, Eben E.  (Eben Eugene), 1848-1916
verses:
My Father, this I ask of Thee;
Knowing that Thou wilt grant the plea,--
For this, and only this, I pray,
Strength for today--just for today.

I do not ask a lifted load,
Nor for a smooth and thornless road;
Simply for strength enough to bear
Life's daily burdens anywhere.

Strength for the present hour and need--
This given, then I'm blest indeed,
For each day, as it comes, will bring
Sufficient strength for anything.

Strength for today, that I may make
Some sad souls glad, for Jesus' sake;
Then they, with me, at eve shall say,
Thank God for strength He gave today.
chorus:
Strength for each trial and each task,
What more, my Father, should I ask?
Just as I need it, day by day,
Strength for my weakness,--this I pray.

title: Just for Today
author: Mary Xavier, Sister, 1856-1917; Wilberforce, Samuel
verses:
Lord, for tomorrow and its needs
I do not pray;
Keep me, my God, from sin
Just for today.
Let me be glad to do Thy will,
Prompt to obey,
Give me Thy helping grace
Just for today.

Keep me from wrong in thought or deed,
O Lord, I pray;
Be near me in my need,
Just for today.
When storm-clouds gather darkly round,
And hide my way.
Be Thou, my light, O Lord,
Just for today.

And when Thy summons comes to me,
Calling away,
Lend me Thy helping hand
Just for today.
So for tomorrow and its needs
I do not pray;
But keep me, guide me, Lord,
Just for today.

title: Just Go On and Do Not Worry
author: Martin, Civilla D. (Civilla Durfee), 1866-1948
verses:
Just go on and do not worry,
Make the best of ev’ry day,
You will often meet with trouble,
Meet with trials on life’s way,
You can always count on Jesus,
He will keep you from all harm,
You may rest in glad assurance
On His everlasting arm.

Just go on and do not worry,
Never murmur or repine,
Tho’ all human help may fail you,
You may trust the pow’r divine,
Tho’ the clouds hang low around you,
Tho’ the storm may seem severe,
He who still’d the raging tempest,
You may always know is near.

Just go on and do not worry,
Let not sin reign in your soul,
Give the Christ, who is your Saviour,
Of your life the full control,
Only in such full surrender,
Can you have God’s very best,
Only as you cease to worry
Can your heart find joy and rest.
chorus:
Just go on and do not worry,
Trusting God, and you will find
That the “peace which passeth understanding,
Shall keep your heart and mind.”

title: Just Judge of Heav'n, against my Foes
author: Hopkinson, Francis, 1737-1791
verses:
Just Judge of Heav'n, against my Foes
Do Thou assert my Right,
Oh set me free, my GOD, from those
Who in Deceit delight;
Since thou'rt my only Stay,
Why mourn I all the Day?
Why leav'st thou me in deep Distress,
While daring Foes my Soul oppress?

Let me with Light and Truth be bless'd,
O let them lead the Way,
'Till on thy holy Hill I rest,
And in thy Temple pray;
Fresh Altars then I'll raise
To GOD; and Songs of Praise
To him, who is my only Joy,
Shall all my grateful Hours employ.

Why then cast down my Soul, and why
So much oppress'd with Care?
On GOD, thy GOD, for Aid rely,
Who will thy State repair:
On him alone depend,
For he's thy surest Friend;
And then his Praise thou yet shalt sing,
Who is thy Health's eternal Spring.

Just lean upon Jesus;
He'll help you along,
And brighten your pathway

Just lean upon Jesus;

title: Just Leave It Alone

verses:
Some doubters are trying God’s Word to revise,
Just leave it alone, just leave it alone,
No longer this line or that passage they prize,
Don’t change it, just leave it alone.

No mortal can better this message of old.
Just leave it alone, just leave it alone,
‘Tis far the best story that ever was told,
Don’t change it, just leave it alone.

‘The army of martyrs” believed ev’ry word,
Just leave it alone, just leave it alone;
The souls of the saints and the sages it stirred,
Don’t change it, just leave it alone.

It’s light is the same as in ages gone by,
Just leave it alone, just leave it alone;
And still its great Give is reigning on high,
Don’t change it, just leave it alone.

Just leave it alone, ‘tis God’s blessed word,

title: Just Like Jesus
author: Jarvis, A. P., Mrs.
verses:
I have a Saviour, O, so kind!
My heart is full of praise,
For He doth give me songs at night
And fills with joy my days.
And when some special good He sends,
Some blessing on my way;
I think how like Him to be kind,
And answer when I pray.

And when He pours His mercies out
Upon my waiting soul;
I thank Him while a grateful wave
Of love doth o’er me roll.
But that is what I should expect
From such a loving friend;
All I can do is yield Him praise,
For blessings He doth send.

‘Twas just like Him to heal the sick,
To cause the blind to see;
To show His love and mercy t’wards
A poor lost soul like me.
And so, when I am worn with care,
When griefs and fears assail,
I take them to the one whose love
And grace doth never fail.
chorus:
‘Tis just like Jesus to answer my pray’r,
‘Tis just like Jesus for my loss to care;
‘Tis just like Jesus my burdens to bear,
And how can I help but love Him.

title: Just Now, O Lord
author: Miles, Ella Elizabeth, 1855-1914
verses:
Just now, O Lord, we need thee,
Just now for help we cry,
Thou art our only refuge,
To thee alone we fly.
Temptations sore beset us,
The flesh indeed is weak,
Within thine arms enfold us,
Their shelter now we seek.

Just now wilt thou receive us,
Nothing to bring have we,
O fill us with thy Spirit,
Our strength and wisdom be.
Alone we cannot conquer
The foes we daily meet,
But, Lord, when thou art with us,
The victory is complete.

Just now, our Father, hear us,
And answer our request,
Free us from Satan's bondage,
From doubts give perfect rest.
Create clean hearts within us,
And pure desires instil;
Let touches of thy mercy,
Our very being thrill.
chorus:
Just now, O Lord, draw near us,
As here we humbly bow;
Incline thine ear and hear us,
And answer, Lord, just now.

title: Just o'er the grave I hung
author: Dwight, Timothy, 1752-1817
verses:
Just o'er the grave I hung--
No pardon met my eyes,
As blessings never greet the slain,
And hope shall never rise.

Sweet mercy to my soul
Reveal'd no charming ray;
Before me rose a long--dark night,
With no succeeding day.

Then--Oh, how vain appear'd
The joys beneath the sky!
Like visions past--like flow'rs that blow
When wint'ry storms are nigh.

How mourn'd my sinking soul
The Sabbath's hours divine,
The day of grace, that precious day,
Consum'd in sense and sin.

The work--the mighty work
Of life, so long delay'd--
Repentance yet to be begun
Upon a dying bed.

When I kneel in His dear presence,

In the quiet even tide;
When He speaks my sin forgiven,
When I in His love abide.

In the twilight shadows dim.

Just one hour with the Saviour,
When the way seems dreary and long;
How it turns all the clouds into sunshine,
The tears into jubilant song.

When the world would lead me away,
Brings His love to my heart in such fullness,
That I from His side would ne’er stray.

Just one hour with the Saviour,

I never fear when night is near 
And hard the hill to climb;
Enough for me if I but see
Just one step at a time.

I'll trust His love sublime,
And press along, with sigh, or song,
Just one step at a time.

His way I choose and shall not lose
The path to that fair clime,
For He will show the way to go,
Just one step at a time.
(Just one step, just one step at a time.)

My trusting soul will reach the goal,
And hear the home bells chime,
Tho' I but see, make bright for me,
Just one step at a time.

title: Just One Thing Have I Desired
author: Paulsen, P. C., (Paul Christian), 1881-1948; Hansen, John
verses:
Just one thing have I desired
Of God, my Father and Lord,
That I may dwell in His temple
And ever be led by His Word.
He hideth me in His pavilion
In times of distress and grief;
He guards me against my pursuers
And gives me rest and relief.

I see His goodness and mercy
And feel His love in my soul;
I know, and yet I must ponder,
The love that my heart has made whole.
I come unto Him as my Father,
Whose heart is most kind and true;
I know He will ever receive me
With loving kindness anew.

I must, while seasons are passing,
Admire the care of my Lord,
Whose hand has always been faithful,
Tho' often I doubted His word,
I linger, and quietly marvel,
In tho'tfulness at His feet:
His goodness endureth forever,
His care is tender and meet.

I lift mine eyes to the mansions
That beckon to me and call,
Which stand on hills everlasting,
When worlds shall crumble and fall.
Just one thing have I desired
And so't after all my days,
That I may abide in His temple
And see His works and His ways.

title: Just One Touch
author: Bell, Birdie
verses:
Just one touch as he moves along,
Pushed and pressed by the jostling throng,
Just one touch, and the weak was strong,
Cured by the Healer divine.

Just one touch and he makes me whole,
Speaks sweet peace to my sin sick soul
At his feet all my burdens roll,
Cured by the Healer divine.

Just one touch!  and the work is done,
I am saved by the blessed Son,
I will sing while the ages run,
Cured by the Healer divine.

Just one touch!  and he turns to me,
O the love in his eyes I see!
I am his for he hears my plea,
Cured by the Healer divine.

Just one touch!  by his mighty pow'r,
He can heal thee this very hour
Thou cans't hear tho' the tempests low'r,
Cured by the Healer divine.
chorus:
Just one touch as he passes by,
He will list to the faintest cry,
Come and be saved while the Lord is nigh,
Christ is the Healer divine.

title: Just One Way
author: Hodge, Arthur J.
verses:
There is just one way for us all to come,
There is just one road that will lead us home,
There is just one gate to the realms of day;
The blessed Jesus is the only way.

There is just one smile that can cheer our path,
There is just one name that can save from wrath,
There is just one life that could e’er atone;
O blessed Jesus, it is Thine alone.

There is just one fount, there is just one cross,
There is just one help for the sinner’s loss,
There is just one hope, all in all to me;
O blessed Jesus, it is not but Thee.
chorus:
Jesus is the way, the only way,
Lovingly He calleth—so the scriptures say—
Whosoever will, let Him come today;
The blessed Jesus is the only way.

title: Just Outside the Door.
author: Rowe, James, 1865-1933

Oh, weary soul, the gate is near,
In sin why still abide?
Both peace and rest are waiting here
And you are just outside.

To save your soul He died;
How can you still offend His heart,
By staying just outside?

The day of life is passing by,
Soon night your soul will hide;
And then "too late" will be your cry,
If you are just outside!

title: Just Over There
author: Libby, James A.
verses:
After this little life of time,
So sorely spent in a world of care,
Cometh for us a life sublime,
And hope keeps singing, "Just over there."

After this little life of time,
Over all earth the curse shall cease;
Robed then as in her sinless prime,
We may find rest in the bowers of peace.

After this little life of time,
We who have waited our King to see,
Blest in a kingdom free from crime,
Sharing His glory shall ever be.

Over beyond this mortal strife,
After the dreamless sleep of death,
Come all the joys of endless life;
Sweetly we cherish what Jesus saith.
chorus:
Never an ill can our pleasure mar,
Just over there where the angels are;
Jesus has said, who has gone before,
We shall be like Him to "die no more."

title: Just over there
author: McPhail, John
verses:
When the heart shall cease to beat,
And the eye, once bright, grows dim,
And the pallid cheek no more its lustre bear,
I shall clasp glad hands with those
Who were once so dear to me,
I shall meet them all again, just over there.

I shall know as I am known,
When around the great white throne,
Far removed beyond the reach of earthly care,
I shall recognize the friends 
Who were precious to me here,
I shall meet them all again, just over there.

I am drawing near the home
Where the weary are at rest,
And I now begin to long the crown to wear,
Soon the loved ones I shall see,
They shall gladly welcome me,
I shall meet them all again, just over there.
chorus:
Just over there, in mansions bright and fair,
Just over there,
Just over there we soon shall meet to part no more,
Just over there,
Just over there.

title: Just Over Yonder
author: Blackmer, F. A. (Francis Augustus), 1855-1930
verses:
There's a better world than this,
Just over yonder;
Just beyond the dark abyss,
Just over yonder.
There are fields of living green,
There decay no more is seen;
Skies unclouded, all serene,
Just over yonder.

There is hope for the opprest,
Just over yonder;
There is joy for the distrest,
Just over yonder.
Grief shall there be felt no more,
Days of weeping all are o'er;
Shadowless immortal shore,
Just over yonder.

We shall meet the loved ones gone,
Just over yonder;
There sweet faces look upon,
Just over yonder.
We shall greet them as of yore,
They will love us as before;
We shall part from them no more,
Just over yonder.

But most wondrous!  I shall see,
Just over yonder,
Him who gave His life for me,
Just over yonder.
Bleeding then on Calvary;
Interceding now for me;
Blessed hope, with Christ to be,
Just over yonder.

title: Just Such a Christ as We Need
author: Carey, A. (Adelaide) Rosalthe, 1841-?
verses:
What a brother we’ve found in the Saviour,
One who never forsakes in our need,
One who feels thro’ His cross ev’ry sorrow,
O He’s just such a Christ as we need.

When we hunger and thirst in life’s desert,
How like manna His promises feed;
And He gives us the cup of salvation,
O He’s just such a Christ as we need.

How He warns wayward souls and entreats them,
How He joys when for mercy they plead;
Ne’er was tempter His grace could not vanquish,
O He’s just such a Christ as we need.

He is one with the Father in glory,
Yet He stoops to our lowliest need;
Never wound was too deep for His healing,
O He’s just such a Christ as we need.
chorus:
Just such a Christ as we need,
Who for the erring will plead,
Who like a shepherd will lead,
Just such a Christ as we need.

title: Just Such a Friend is Jesus
author: Morris, C. H., Mrs. 1862-1929
verses:
Oh, who has not felt that the cares of earth
Were more than man's strength could bear,
And longed for a friend who could understand,
And all of life's burdens share?

Oh, who has not felt the dark stain of sin
Like crimson upon his soul,
And sought for a friend who had pow'r to free
From passions which held control?

When those that we love have been snatched away,
And walk no more by our side,
Oh, where is the One who will dearer be
Than all of earth's friends beside?

Thou Friend of the friendless, so kind and true,
Thou Savior of sinners lost,
Protect us and guide us life's journey thro'
Till safely death's stream we've crossed.
chorus:
Just such a Friend is Jesus,
Just such a Friend is Jesus:
His grace doth forever to sinners abound;
Just such a Friend is Jesus.

title: Just Take His Hand
author: Rowe, James, 1865-1933
verses:
When storms of life are raging and the way you cannot see,
Or when your burden causes you to fall,
Let not your heart be troubled, do not let your courage flee;
Just take the hand of Jesus, that is all.

When sorrow overtakes you, tho’ your friends from you depart,
Unmindful of your pleading sigh or call,
Let not your faith decrease, but keep a peaceful, trusting heart,
And take the hand of Jesus, that is all.

When comes at last the summons, and the silent stream you see,
Let not the swelling waves your soul appall;
Remembering his promises, still true and fearless be,
And take the hand of Jesus, that is all.

title: Just the Case for Him
author: Habershon, Ada R. (Ada Ruth), 1861-1918
verses:
In the dark without a light,
Blind, but longing for my sight,
Always vanquished in the fight,—
Just the case for Him.

Lost, and wand’ring from the way,
Bankrupt, with my debts to pay,
Guilty, and with naught to say,—
Just the case for Him.

Burdens much too hard to bear,
Only filthy rags to wear,
Many griefs, and none to care,—
Just the case for Him.

Tossed upon the billow’s crest,
With no place where I can rest,
Safe at last upon His breast,—
Just the case for Him.

Coming with my ev’ry need,
Having nothing good to plead,
Yet I know I am indeed,—
Just the case for Him.
chorus:

Just the case for Him;
Coming with my ev’ry need,
Just the case for Him.

He’s just the Friend I need.

He’s just the Friend I need;

He’s just the Friend I need.
He lifted me from depths of woe,

He’s just the Friend I need;
A present help I find in Him,
He’s just the Friend I need.
When all this changing life is o’er,
And I have gained the Homeland shore,
I’ll sing His praise forevermore,
He’s just the Friend I need.

Just the love of Jesus, just the love of Jesus!

Just the love of Jesus, my Savior!

What will help me triumph in this earthly strife?
Just the love of Jesus, just the love of Jesus!

title: Just to Be With My Lord
author: Jackson, Lyman F.
verses:
Just to be with the Lord whom I adore!
Just to worship at his feet!
Just to sing to his praise as ne’er before,
If for such a service meet.

Just to sit at his feet and learn of him,
What, before, I could not know!
See him, not thro’ a glass by shadows dim,
As I see him here below!

Just to grow, in the brightness of his face,
More like him as ages roll!
Just to stand as a triumph of his grace,
And his wondrous love extol!

Just to know, gracious Lord, thy blessed will,
And to do it day by day;
Just my place in the harvest field to fill,
While I labor, love and pray!

Thro’ the grace bestowed in love;
So to live and thy love to others show,
I may dwell with thee above.

title: Just to Please Jesus

Paying a visit to sorrow’s abode,
Helping a burdened one o’er a rough road;
This the sweet tho’t, making duty delight,
Turning the shadows of gloom into light,
Just to please Jesus,
Just to please Jesus.

Staying at home with the children, perchance,
Watching the sick one oft-wandering glace,
Sweeping and dusting, and tidying home,
Deeds not recorded ‘neath Fame’s painted dome,
Just to please Jesus,
Just to please Jesus.

Swinging the hammer if duty demands,
Plying the needle with quick willing hands,
Using the pencil, the pick, or the pen,
Serving my Lord and my own fellow men,
Just to please Jesus,
Just to please Jesus.

Jesus my Savior! my Helper is He;
Just to see Jesus fill heaven with gladness,

title: Justice and equity
author: Watts, Isaac, 1674-1748
verses:
Blessed redeemer how divine,
How righteous is this rule of thine,
"Never to deal with others worse
"Than we would have them deal with us!"

This golden lesson, short and plain,
Gives nor the mind nor memory pain:
And every conscience must approve
This universal law of love.

'Tis written in each mortal breast,
Where all our tenderest wishes rest:
We draw it from our inmost veins,
Where love to self resides and reigns.

Is reason ever at a loss?
Call in self-love to judge the cause:
Let our own fondest passions shew
How we should treat our neighbor too.

How bless'd would every nation prove,
Thus rul'd by equity and love!
All would be friends without a foe,
And form a paradise below.

Jesus, forgive us, that we keep
Thy sacred law of love asleep;
And take our envy, wrath, and pride,
Those savage passions, for our guide.

title: Justification
author: Wesley, John, 1703-1791
verses:
Lord, thy imputed righteousness
My beauty is, my glorious dress;
'Midst flaming worlds in this array'd,
With joy shall I lift up my head.

When from the dust of death I rise,
To take my mansion in the skies,
E'en then shall this be all my plea,
"Jesus hath liv'd and dy'd for me."

Bold shall I stand in that great day,
For who aught to my charge shall lay?
While thro' thy blood absolv'd I am,
From sin's tremendous curse and shame.

Thus Abraham the friend of God,
Thus all the armies bought with blood,
By faith on thee alone relied,
And in the Lord were justified.

This spotless robe the same appears
When ruin'd nature sinks in years:
No age can change its glorious hue,
The robe of Christ is ever new.

O! let the dead now hear thy voice!
Bid, Lord, thy mourning ones rejoice;
Their beauty this, their glorious dress,
"Jesus, the Lord our righteousness."

Jesus is the one to help us on the way,
Keep looking unto him,
Keep looking unto him;
Overcoming strength he gives from day to day,
Keep looking unto Jesus all the way.

When the eye of faith cannot discern the right,
Keep looking unto him,
Keep looking unto him;
He will make the path of duty clear and bright,
Keep looking unto Jesus all the way.

When the storms are raging fiercely overhead,
Keep looking unto him,
Keep looking unto him;
Great with mercy are the clouds we so much dread,
Keep looking unto Jesus all the way.

Would we gain a home with Jesus evermore,
Keep looking unto him,
Keep looking unto him;
Would we safely land upon the heav’nly shore,
Keep looking unto Jesus all the way.
chorus:
Keep looking unto him,
Keep looking unto him,
Looking unto Jesus all the way;
He’s the only one to help us day by day,
Keep looking unto Jesus all the way.

title: Keep Looking Unto Jesus
author: Owens, Priscilla J., 1829-1907
verses:
Keep looking unto Jesus as we march along,
Keep looking unto Jesus all the day,
When our hopes are steadfast and our hearts are strong,
We can tread the narrow way.

Keep looking unto Jesus with the night around,
Keep looking unto Jesus, Star and Sun.
We shall yet behold him with full glory crowned,
When the final vict’ry’s won.

Keep looking unto Jesus, Author of our faith,
Keep looking unto Jesus as we move,
We shall share his triumph over sin and death,
We shall reign with him above.
chorus:
Keep looking unto Jesus, looking unto Jesus,
Looking unto Jesus ev’ry day.
Till our cares grow lighter and our hopes grow brighter,
And our sorrows flee away.

title: Keep Looking Unto Jesus
author: Buffum, Herbert, 1879-1939
verses:
Would you understand the secret of the overcomer’s life?
Keep looking unto Jesus all the way;
Would you come off more than conqu’ror in the midst of ev’ry strife,
Keep looking unto Jesus all the way.

When the enemy assaileth when the tempter presses sore,
Keep looking unto Jesus all the way;
Just remember where sin doth abound His grace aboundeth more,
Keep looking unto Jesus all the way.

And when you behold the Jordan flowing there in front of you,
Keep looking unto Jesus all the way;
Just keep looking unto Jesus He will bear you safely thro’,
Keep looking unto Jesus all the way.
chorus:
Keep looking,
Keep looking,
Keep looking unto Jesus all the way.
Keep looking,
Keep looking,
Keep looking unto Jesus all the way.

title: Keep Marching On
author: Mackay, J. B.
verses:
We are marching at the call of God,
On to glory, on to glory;
We have girded on the gospel sword,
Soon to wear a crown.

Marching on against the hosts of sin,
On to glory, on to glory;
Be stout-hearted, we will surely win,
Soon to wear a crown.

In the battle we shall fear no harm,
On to glory, on to glory;
We are shielded by a mighty arm,
Soon to wear a crown.

March till ev’ry foe is put to flight,
On to glory, on to glory;
Doing battle for the truth, the right,
Soon to wear a crown.
chorus:
March on,
And we shall shout the victory;
March on,
And we shall gain the day.

title: Keep Me as the Apple of the Eye
author: Herbert, J. B. (John Bunyan), 1852-1927
verses:
Hold up my goings, Lord, me guide
In paths that are divine,
That so my footsteps may not slide
Out of those ways of Thine.

Upon Thee I have called, O God,
Because Thou wilt me hear;
That Thou mayst hearken to my speech,
To me incline Thy ear.

Thy wondrous loving-kindness show,
Thou, who by Thy right hand
Dost save all those who trust in Thee
From such as them withstand.
chorus:
Keep me as the apple of the eye,
Hide me under the shadow of Thy wings;
Keep me as the apple of the eye,
Hide me under the shadow of Thy wings.

title: Keep Me, Blessed Saviour
author: Morton, Jennie
verses:
Keep me, blessed Savior, keep me
In thy loving care;
May I, in the time of sorrow,
Find a refuge there.

Keep me, blessed Savior, keep me
Safe from all alarms;
When the storms of life are raging,
Safe within thine arms.

Keep me, blessed Savior, keep me
Near thy bleeding side;
When the tempter’s pow’r assails me,
May I there abide.

Keep me, blessed Savior, keep me
Till this life is o’er;
Then be thou the first to greet me
On the heav’nly shore.
chorus:
Keep me, blessed Savior, keep me,
Safely evermore;
Stay beside me all the journey,
Till I reach the golden shore.

title: Keep me Ever
author: Crosby, Fanny, 1820-1915
verses:
In Thy perfect peace divine,
Keep, O keep me ever;
Where my faith will brightest shine,
Keep, O keep me ever.

At my post of duty still
Keep, O keep me ever;
Learning there Thy righteous will,
Keep, O keep me ever.

‘Neath Thy all protecting wings,
Keep, O keep me ever;
By the soul refreshing springs,
Keep, O keep me ever.

Till my last expiring breath,
Keep, O keep me ever;
Thine in life, and Thine in death,
Keep, O keep me ever.
chorus:
Let Thy heart my dwelling be,
Let Thy word abide in me;
In the path that leads to Thee,
Keep, O keep me ever.
